# tritonctl

> tritonctl is the tenant CLI for Triton Cloud. This guide is for coding
> agents that drive it from a shell. Most of it is about sandboxes:
> Linux microVMs that run programs, hold files and serve preview URLs.
> The same commands also manage instances, networks and storage.

## Setup

- Config lives in `~/.config/triton/tritonctl/`, or in
  `$TRITONCTL_CONFIG_DIR` when set. Use a temporary directory there to
  keep a script away from the user's session.
- Log in once:
  `tritonctl configure --endpoint <URL> --project <PROJECT> --username <USER> --password-stdin`
  reads the password from stdin. `tritonctl login` signs in again
  (`--sso` for a browser sign-in). `tritonctl whoami` shows who you are.
- Without a stored session: `TRITONCTL_ENDPOINT` with `TRITONCTL_API_KEY`
  (make one with `tritonctl api-key create`) or `TRITONCTL_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
- A private CA for the API: `TRITON_DC_ANCHORS=<ca.pem>`.
- `-p <PROFILE>` picks a stored profile; `--project` overrides the
  project for one command.
- `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `completion` and `--help` need no session.

## Sandboxes

A sandbox is named by name, uuid or uuid prefix. Every sandbox has a
deadline (`--ttl`); `keepalive` moves it later.

- Create and wait until it runs:
  `tritonctl sandbox create --name dev --ttl 1h`. Size it with
  `--cpu 2 --memory 2G --disk 8G`. `--template <NAME>` picks the image.
  `--on-deadline stop|pause|delete` sets what the deadline does.
- Run a program: `tritonctl sandbox exec dev -- make test`. The exit
  status is the program's own. `--cmd '<shell line>'` runs a shell line,
  `--cwd`, `--env K=V` and `--max-duration 10m` as named. Add `-q` to get
  only the program's output. `-t -i` is an interactive terminal; do not
  use it from a script. `--tag <TAG>` and `exec-attach dev <TAG>`
  reattach to a long run.
- Files: `tritonctl sandbox fs put dev ./a.csv /work/a.csv`, `fs get`,
  `fs cat`, `fs ls`, `fs stat`, `fs mv`, `fs mkdir`, `fs rm`,
  `fs watch dev /work`.
- Ports: start a server in the guest, then
  `tritonctl sandbox url dev 8000` prints its preview URL with a
  one-time token. `tritonctl sandbox ports ls dev` lists ports;
  `tritonctl sandbox ports open dev 8000 --public` drops the token
  (gated). `tritonctl sandbox port-forward dev 5432` forwards a local TCP
  port.
- Snapshot and fork: `tritonctl sandbox snapshot create dev --name ready`,
  then `tritonctl sandbox fork dev --count 3 --from-snapshot ready`.
  `--kind memory` keeps running processes too (gated).
- Stop and start keep the disk, not the memory:
  `tritonctl sandbox stop dev`, `tritonctl sandbox start dev`.
  `tritonctl sandbox pause dev` and `tritonctl sandbox resume dev` keep
  memory and disk (gated).
- Templates: `tritonctl sandbox template build py312 --image docker.io/library/python:3.12-slim --follow`.
  `--dockerfile <FILE> --context <DIR>` (gated) or
  `--from-snapshot dev/ready` also work. Then
  `tritonctl sandbox create --name t1 --template py312`.
  `tritonctl sandbox template list` lists them.
- Code interpreter: use an SDK (Python `triton_sandbox`, TypeScript
  `triton-sandbox`) with `template="code-interpreter"` and
  `sbx.run_code(...)`. The SDKs read the tritonctl session.
- Desktop (gated): `tritonctl sandbox create --name desk --template desktop`,
  then `tritonctl sandbox rdp desk` and connect an RDP client to
  `127.0.0.1:13389`.
- Network: egress is denied by default.
  `--allow-out <CIDR>` and `--allow-out-domain <NAME>` (gated) on
  create open it; `tritonctl sandbox network show dev` shows the policy and
  `tritonctl sandbox network replace dev ...` replaces all of it. Private
  ranges are always refused. Egress needs a NAT gateway in the VPC.
- GitHub: `tritonctl sandbox create --name app --repo owner/app` clones
  into `/work/app` with the token from `gh auth token`. Then
  `tritonctl sandbox git app -- switch -c fix`,
  `tritonctl sandbox git app -- commit -am "Fix"` and
  `tritonctl sandbox pr app --title "Fix" --draft`.
  `tritonctl sandbox ssh-config app --install` adds an ssh_config entry
  for ssh, scp and editors.
- Claude Code: `tritonctl sandbox claude` runs it in a sandbox named
  `claude`, with the key from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`
  or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. `--repo owner/app`
  clones first.
- `tritonctl sandbox capability` shows what this deployment offers. A
  gated feature that is off answers `FeatureDisabled`; ask the
  administrator to turn it on.
- Clean up: `tritonctl sandbox delete -y dev`.

## Output

- Lists are tables with a header row; `-H` drops the header, `-o a,b`
  picks columns, `-s col` sorts.
- `-j` (or `--format json`) prints the raw records as JSON. This is the
  stable interface for scripts; parse it, not the table.
- `exec` prints the program's output as it runs, and one summary line on
  stderr (`-q` drops it).

## Errors and exit codes

Errors go to stderr as `tritonctl <command>: error (<Code>): <message>`,
sometimes with a hint line. `-v` adds the cause chain.

- 0: ok
- 1: failure (server fault, refused change, ambiguous name)
- 2: bad usage, or a prompt with no terminal
- 3: not found
- 4: no session, or not allowed
- `sandbox exec`: the program's exit status, or 128 plus the signal

## Safe patterns

- Deletes and other changes ask `[y/N]`. In a script, pass `-y`; with no
  terminal and no `-y` the command exits 2. `-n` (`--dry-run`) prints the
  plan and stops.
- `sandbox create`, `start` and `resume` wait until the sandbox runs.
  Keep that; `--no-wait` returns before the sandbox can take an exec.
  `template build` takes `--wait` or `--follow`.
- Give each sandbox a short `--ttl`, so a script that dies leaves nothing
  behind.
- Name things you make (`--name`) and use the name after, not a prefix
  that may match two things.
- Read, then change: `show -j` before `update`, `network show` before
  `network replace`.
